# GoldHEN Plugins
Plugins allows you to customize your games like never before!

[![Build modules](https://github.com/GoldHEN/GoldHEN_Plugins_Repository/actions/workflows/CI.yml/badge.svg?branch=main&event=push)](https://github.com/GoldHEN/GoldHEN_Plugins_Repository/actions/workflows/CI.yml)

## Features:

- Hook into Games before boot.
- Write your own code into games in C/C++.
- Hook and modify system functions.

## :warning: Disclaimer

While we make every effort to deliver high quality products, we do not guarantee that our products are free from defects. Our software is provided **as is** and you use the software at your own risk.

# Quick Start

- Load [GoldHEN 2.3](https://github.com/GoldHEN/GoldHEN/releases/latest) or newer on your PS4.
- Enable option to load plugins in Plugins Menu.
- Download plugins from [Release Page](https://github.com/GoldHEN/GoldHEN_Plugins_Repository/releases/latest).
- Extract downloaded plugins into `/data/GoldHEN/plugins/`.
- Add plugins you want to load into `/data/GoldHEN/plugins.ini`.
  - Per game plugins sections are recommended over putting everything in `default`.

```ini
; Load plugins for any title

[default]
/data/GoldHEN/plugins/game_patch.prx

; Load plugins only for Playroom

[CUSA00001]
/data/GoldHEN/plugins/afr.prx
/data/GoldHEN/plugins/no_share_watermark.prx
```

## Plugins

### AFR (Application File Redirector)

Plugin filename: `afr.prx`

Author(s):
- [SiSTR0](https://github.com/SiSTR0)
- [jocover](https://github.com/jocover)

Redirect file calls to `/data/`

<details>
<summary>How To Use (Click to Expand)</summary>

- Create a folder in `/data`
  - `/data/GoldHEN/AFR/(title id)/`
- Place files into newly created `(title id)` folder
  - Example for `CUSA00001` `/app0/hello_afr.txt` -> `/data/GoldHEN/AFR/CUSA00001/hello_afr.txt`
- Run your game.

</details>

### Button Swap

Plugin filename: `button_swap.prx`

Author(s):
- [jocover](https://github.com/jocover)

Swap X and O around on Asia Region console.

### Force 1080p Display

Plugin filename: `force_1080p_display.prx`

Author(s):
- [illusion](https://github.com/illusion0001)

Reports to the app that it is connected to a 1080p display.

### Force 30 FPS

Plugin filename: `force_30_fps.prx`

Author(s):
- [illusion](https://github.com/illusion0001)

Force any game to run at 30 FPS.

### Fliprate Remover

Plugin filename: `fliprate_remover.prx`

Author(s):
- [illusion](https://github.com/illusion0001)

Removes framerate limit for games using system function `sceVideoOutSetFlipRate`.

### FrameTime Logger

Plugin filename: `frame_logger.prx`

Author(s):
- [illusion](https://github.com/illusion0001)

  - Log frametime statistics.
  - Press `L3 + L1 + Triangle` to start capturing data.
  - Press `L3 + R3 + L1 + R1 + Square` to stop plugin.
  - Logs data to `/data/frame_logger/`.

### GamePad helper Plugin

# DayBreak V1.1.2 – BO3 Zombies SPRX (PS4 / PS5)

**Game:** Black Ops III – CUSA02290 (V1.33)
**Needs:** GoldHEN (PS4) or NexHEN (PS5)

Lan Spoof Works on MP/ZM/CP

link to keep checking if it gets updated download new file
https://github.com/xexpoiiison/DayBreak-SPRX-Release

## Fixed in V1.1.2
- **Set Round now sticks.** Picking a round jumped to current+1 instead (round 2 → 3). It now sets BO3's real round counter, so it lands on the round you pick.
- **Pack-a-Punch Current Weapon** now works on guns the map's upgrade table misses, like the **Razorback**.

## Fixed in V1.1.1
- **PS5 / NexHEN autoload:** DayBreak didn't show up when set to `?autoload=true` in NexHEN (no load box, no menu), but worked when loaded from the Plugin Loader at the main menu. NexHEN autoload injects the moment the game starts, before BO3 is ready, and DayBreak gave up. It now waits for the main menu and hooks in then, the same as the Plugin Loader. It also keeps retrying its startup and controller hook instead of giving up, and shows the load box within 20 seconds on the main menu even if the X on "Press X to start" was missed.
- **Clearer messages:** if another plugin already hooked BO3 or took over the controller, DayBreak now says so instead of "game version doesn't match".
- PS4 with GoldHEN loads the same as before.

## Install (PS4 – GoldHEN)
1. Download `DayBreak.sprx`
2. With FTP, copy it to:
   `/data/GoldHEN/plugins/DayBreak.sprx`
3. Open `/data/GoldHEN/plugins.ini` (create it if it isn't there) and add:
   ```ini
   [CUSA02290]
   /data/GoldHEN/plugins/DayBreak.sprx
   ```
4. Restart BO3.

## Install (PS5 – NexHEN)
1. Download `DayBreak.sprx`
2. With FTP, copy it to:
   `/data/nexHEN/plugins/DayBreak.sprx`
3. In NexHEN's `plugins.ini`, add:
   ```ini
   [CUSA02290]
   /data/nexHEN/plugins/DayBreak.sprx?autoload=true
   ```
   Or leave off `?autoload=true` and enable it through NexHEN's Plugin Loader.
4. Start BO3.

## Use
- After "Press X to start" it asks **"Would you like to load DayBreak ZM SPRX?"** Pick **Yes**.
- **L1 + R1** opens the menu (Pre Game Menu on the main menu, Full Menu in a match).
- **D-pad** moves, **X** selects, **O** goes back, **Left / Right** changes values.
- **Verified players:** hold **L1** and tap **R1** (or **L1 + Triangle**) to open their menu.

## Coming in V1.2
- **Stats for all modes** (Multiplayer, Campaign and Zombies), done right in the SPRX, no GSC injection: level, prestige, unlocks, liquid divinium, clan tag and more.

## Problems
- Nothing shows up: check the path and `plugins.ini`, and make sure your game is CUSA02290 on the latest patch.
- Running other BO3 plugins? Try DayBreak by itself first, and only list it once in `plugins.ini`.
- Questions: Discord / X **@xexpoiiison**

Created By: XeX Poiiison

core/: derived from Xenia Canary (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) 2015 Ben Vanik and the
Xenia contributors); the PS5 changes are MIT like the rest of PS5X360.
helper/: PS5X360 Helper. Its own files are MIT. The payload links the PS5 payload SDK
adapter of John Tornblom (GPL-3.0-or-later) and Mbed TLS (Apache-2.0); see
helper/native/autolog/README.md. No PS5SX2 code is included: the design follows the
PS5SX2 installer's documented behaviour.

# PS5X360 Updater 1.0.0

`PS5X360-Updater.elf` is an ordinary PS5 payload. Send it with your ELF loader (port 9021) whenever you want
PS5X360 brought up to date. Each time it runs it:

1. reads the installed build from `/data/homebrew/PPSA50011/VERSION`;
2. asks GitHub for the latest release of `BrinooTk/PS5X360` (over HTTPS, certificate and host name checked);
3. stops there when that release is not newer ("PS5X360 is up to date", or "newer than the latest release" for a
   test build);
4. otherwise downloads the release's `PPSA50011.zip` and checks its size and the SHA-256 GitHub publishes for it;
5. unpacks it into `updater/stage/` beside the installation, checking every file against the zip's CRC-32 and
   the package's own `MANIFEST.json` (SHA-256 per file);
6. waits up to 20 minutes for PS5X360 to be closed ("close PS5X360 to install it") and then puts the files in place,
   `eboot.bin` last.

Notifications on the PS5 tell each step, in Portuguese on a console set to Portuguese and in English otherwise.
The full story is in `/data/homebrew/PPSA50011/updater/updater.log`.

## What it changes

| Files | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Files in the release (`eboot.bin`, `sce_sys`, `sce_module`, `assets`, licences, notes) | Replaced. A replaced file that differs from the new one is kept in `updater/backup/<previous version>/`. |
| Settings in the release (`*.conf`, `*.toml`, `*.ini`, `assets/presets.txt`) that you changed | Kept. The new copy is written beside it as `<name>.new`. A file is "yours" when it matches neither the previous build's `MANIFEST.json` nor the new file. |
| Everything else (games, saves, logs, caches, DLC, title updates, your own files) | Never touched. Nothing is ever deleted from the installation. |

Only the two newest backups are kept. Downloads and unpacked copies of releases that are not being installed are
removed on the next run.

**Power cut or crash half-way:** the install is recorded in `updater/install.txt` before the first file moves, and
files only move by renaming checked copies on the same drive. The next run finishes the install from
`updater/stage/`. Until `eboot.bin` (the last file) is in place, the previous executable still starts.

**Won't install when:** PS5X360 stays open for 20 minutes (send the updater again later); the release has no
published SHA-256; the download or a file in it does not match; there is not enough free space (the unpacked size
plus 128 MB); another copy of the updater is running.

## Switches

Empty files in `/data/homebrew/PPSA50011/updater/`:

- `no-update`: do nothing.
- `force`: install the latest release even when it is not newer (for example, to go back from a test build). It is
  used once (renamed `force.used`).
- `check-only`: download, check and unpack, but install nothing.
- `beta`: also consider pre-releases.
- `test-root` (one line, a folder path containing "test"): install into that folder instead (console tests).

## Inside the PS5X360 Helper

The same code is also built into the PS5X360 Helper (`native/autolog`, Helper 1.2.0) as a module:
`native/autolog/helper_update.c` compiles `updater.c` with `UPD_MODULE`, and the Helper calls the functions in
`updater_module.h`. The flow, rules, switches, log and state folder are the ones above. The differences:

- a release ready while PS5X360 is open stays staged instead of waited for; the Helper looks every 5 s and installs
  it once PS5X360 is closed, with no 20-minute limit. If PS5X360 is opened while files are being placed, the
  journal finishes the install on a later look;
- a check at load that cannot reach GitHub is tried again by the Helper without a failure notification, except for
  the last try;
- the Helper's HTTPS requests take turns with the AutoLog collector's (one Mbed TLS state per process), and the
  collector supplies the entropy source.

Host builds also accept `UPDATER_FAKE_GITHUB=<folder>`: addresses are answered from files in that folder (named after
the address's last part) instead of HTTPS, for the Helper's tests. `UPDATER_CLOSE_GRACE` sets the pause after
PS5X360 closes (3 s). The PS5 build has neither.

## Build and test

Needs the AutoLog collector's Mbed TLS 3.6.7 (`.deps/autolog/mbedtls-3.6.7`) and its generated CA roots and library
(`build/autolog-native/roots.h`, `libmbedtls.a`; `tools/build-native-autolog.sh`).

Y2JB Installer for Windows
==========================

This ZIP contains one executable. There is nothing to install; double-click
y2jb-installer.exe.

Requirements
------------
- Windows 10 (1803 or later) or Windows 11.
- Microsoft Edge WebView2. It is built into Windows 11 and installed with
  Edge on Windows 10. If it is missing, install the Evergreen WebView2
  Runtime from Microsoft.
- The PS5 must be on firmware 4.03-13.60, with kernel read/write access and
  an ELF loader listening on port 9021. Firmware 11.40 is not supported by
  the Y2JB autoloader.

No administrator rights, WSL, MSYS2, Python or .NET are needed. The
executable carries its own runtime except for WebView2, which is part of
Windows.

First launch
------------
Windows SmartScreen will warn that the app is unsigned. Choose "More info",
then "Run anyway". The build is not code-signed.

Where data is kept
------------------
Downloads and settings live in:

    %APPDATA%\dev.y2jb.installer

Delete that folder to reclaim the space or start fresh. Remove the app by
deleting the executable.

Before launching YouTube
------------------------
Disconnect the console from the internet first. Opening YouTube online can
show the sign-in screen and overwrite download0.dat, which breaks the Y2JB
setup and requires reinstalling it.

Safety
------
The app talks to Sony's package servers and GitHub from this PC, and to the
console on your local network. It does not contain an exploit. The payload it
sends runs only on a console that already has kernel read/write access.

# Y2JB

Userland code execution using the PS5 YouTube app.

## Requirements

- At least 4.03 firmware PS5

### For Jailbroken PS5 (Webkit, Lua, BD-JB)
- Fake or legit activated PS5
- For firmware 4.03 to 12.40 get YouTube app (PPSA01650) version 01.000.003 PKG
- For firmware 12.60 and up get YouTube app (PPSA01650) version 01.000.030 PKG
- FTP access to the console

### For Non-Jailbroken PS5
- USB flash drive
- Pre-made backup file

## Setup Instructions

### Configure Network DNS Settings (Optional, but highly recommended)

1. Navigate to **Settings > Network > Settings > Set Up Internet Connection**
2. Scroll to the bottom and select **Set Up Manually**
3. Choose your connection type:
   - **Use WiFi**: Enter your network name and password manually, then set security to "WPA-Personal..."
   - **Use a LAN Cable**: Proceed to the next step
4. Under **DNS Settings**, change from "Automatic" to **Manual**
5. Set **Primary DNS** to `127.0.0.2` (leave Secondary DNS blank)
6. Press **Done** and wait for the connection to establish

**Note:** You may see a network/PSN connection error - this is expected and can be safely ignored. The console will still function normally for YouTube payload delivery.

**Alternative:** Instead of using 127.0.0.2, you can block PSN servers using your custom DNS server.

#### Why is Setting DNS to 127.0.0.2 Required?

The DNS configuration is critical for Y2JB to function properly for two technical reasons:

1. **Blocking PSN Connections**: Setting the DNS to 127.0.0.2 (localhost) prevents the PS5 from reaching PlayStation Network servers. This blocks both the YouTube app and system firmware update prompts that would otherwise interfere with the exploit.

### Fake Account Activation

**Note:** If you're using the backup file from the releases page, you can skip this section.

Y2JB requires a **fake-activated account** to run properly.

**Important:** If you have a legit PSN-activated account (officially registered through PlayStation Network), you **cannot** use it directly with Y2JB. You must create and use a separate fake-activated account instead.

**To fake activate an account:**
1. Create a new offline account on your PS5
2. While logging in to this new account, open **etaHEN toolbox**
3. Navigate to the **"Remote Play"** menu
4. The account will be automatically fake activated

### Jailbroken PS5

1. Install YouTube app PKG on your PS5
2. Download `download0.dat` from the releases page.
3. Transfer `download0.dat` with [Prospero Manager](https://github.com/notmaj0r/ProsperoMgr), [FTP](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/ftpsrv), or any file manager to the path matching your YouTube app's TITLE ID (create the folder if it does not exist):
   ```
   /user/download/PPSA01650
   /user/download/PPSA01651
   /user/download/PPSA01652
   ```
   You only need to use one path. Choose the one matching your YouTube app's TITLE ID.

### Non-Jailbroken PS5

1. Download the backup file from the releases page  
**Firmware 4.03 – 12.40** → `Y2JB_backup_1.6(4.03)`  
**Firmware 12.60 and up** → `Y2JB_backup_1.6(12.20)`  
2. Follow Sony's official guide to [restore backup data from USB](https://www.playstation.com/en-gb/support/hardware/back-up-ps5-data-USB/)

**⚠️ WARNING:** Restoring backup data **WILL FACTORY RESET YOUR PS5**. All data on your console will be erased.

### Blocking YouTube Updates (appinfo_editor.py)

**⚠️ CRITICAL WARNING:** Database corruption can result in the deletion of **ALL installed FPKGs and savedata** stored on your internal storage. Before proceeding with this section, **backup your savedata** using the PS5's built-in backup and restore feature in Settings to prevent data loss.

This script prevents the YouTube app from updating if you accidentally connect to the internet. Allowing updates can cause a softlock that prevents YouTube from launching (see next section for fix instructions).  

**Steps:**
1. After installing the YouTube PKG, retrieve `/system_data/priv/mms/appinfo.db` from your PS5 using FTP
2. Place `appinfo.db` in the same directory as `appinfo_editor.py`
3. Run the script to modify `appinfo.db` and block YouTube updates:
   ```
   python appinfo_editor.py
   ```
4. **Before replacing the file** on your PS5 (to avoid database corruption):
   - Close the YouTube app completely
   - Navigate to the Settings page
   - Ensure no packages are currently being installed or updated
5. Use FTP to replace `/system_data/priv/mms/appinfo.db` with the modified version
6. If you don't receive any database corruption notification, reboot your PS5

### How to Escape from YouTube Softlock
![youtube_softlock](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62012e7f-e004-4e20-8c18-bd7d0bbd72b1)

This issue typically occurs when you connect to the internet **before** setting the 127.0.0.2 DNS (most common with WiFi users).

**Recovery steps:**
1. Once softlocked, connect to the internet normally without custom DNS
2. Launch YouTube again and deny the system software update popup
3. The YouTube app should now launch successfully
4. Run the jailbreak and load HEN
5. Set the DNS to 127.0.0.2 again, then uninstall YouTube
6. Follow the **Jailbroken PS5** section and **Blocking YouTube Updates (appinfo_editor.py)** section again
7. Restart your PS5. Done.

## Sending Payloads

**Note:** The Remote JS Server does not always use port 50000. While it typically defaults to port 50000, it may occasionally use a different port - this is normal behavior, not a bug.

You can send payloads using `payload_sender.py` (requires Python).

**Usage:**
```
python payload_sender.py <host> <file>
python payload_sender.py <host> <port> <file>
```

**Examples:**
```
python payload_sender.py 192.168.1.100 helloworld.js
python payload_sender.py 192.168.1.100 50000 helloworld.js
python payload_sender.py 192.168.1.100 9020 payload.bin
```

### Lapse Payload

**Firmware Compatibility:** Only works up to firmware 10.01

After the Lapse payload succeeds, you need to send the HEN or other elf binary to port **9021**. You can use any TCP payload sender such as:
- `netcat`
- `payload_sender.py`

**Example:**
```
python payload_sender.py 192.168.1.100 9021 hen.bin
```

### Relapse Payload

**Firmware Compatibility:** Works up to firmware 13.60
- Requires an active network connection (Wi-Fi or Ethernet). 

After the Relapse payload succeeds, elfldr starts listening on port **9021**.

# Y2JB Installer

A cross-platform application that prepares a PlayStation 5 for **Y2JB**. It handles account activation, fake PSN sign-in, YouTube installation, `download0.dat` placement, and blocking YouTube updates. It runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.

This project does not include an exploit. The console only needs kernel read/write access from a compatible exploit; once `download0.dat` is in place, launching YouTube starts Y2JB.

> **Unsigned desktop builds.** Desktop artifacts are not signed with an Apple Developer ID or a Windows code-signing certificate. macOS requires a first-launch confirmation, and Windows SmartScreen displays a warning. The Android APK is self-signed for sideloading. See [Installation](#installation).

## Overview

Y2JB Installer consists of two cooperating components:

- **Application** — a Tauri 2 / Svelte 5 application for desktop and Android that owns the interface, performs all internet access, downloads and verifies files, and uploads them to the console.
- **PS5 payload** — a small C HTTP service that runs on the console and performs the privileged operations: uploads, YouTube installation, account activation, fake sign-in, `download0.dat` placement, and `appinfo.db` patching.

The console does not need outbound internet access. The application fetches Sony packages and GitHub assets, verifies them, and transfers the results over the local network.

## Features

- Offline local account activation and fake PSN sign-in.
- Firmware-aware YouTube build selection for firmware **4.03 – 13.60**. The [Y2JB autoloader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-y2jb-autoloader) does not support **11.40**.
- Verified Sony PKG downloads, package joining, and installation.
- `download0.dat` release selection with local/console version reporting and update detection.
- In-place YouTube update blocking with timestamped `appinfo.db` backups.
- LAN discovery and manual console connection.
- Local download cache with per-artifact status and cleanup.
- System-aware light and dark themes.

Each setup step is independent and can be repeated safely.

## Requirements

### Console

- PS5 on firmware **4.03 – 13.60**. The Y2JB autoloader does not support firmware **11.40**.
- Kernel read/write access from a compatible exploit.
- An ELF loader listening on TCP port **9021** (elfdr or equivalent).

### Desktop

- Windows 10 1803+ or Windows 11, with the WebView2 runtime.
- macOS 11 or later.
- Linux with glibc 2.35+ (Ubuntu 22.04 baseline), x64 or arm64, plus WebKitGTK 4.1, GTK 3, librsvg, and libappindicator.
- Internet access and a network route to the console.
- No administrator rights are required on Windows.

The AppImage is not fully self-contained; it uses the host glibc and graphical runtime
libraries. It is built against the Ubuntu 22.04 baseline.

### Android

- Android 7.0 or later; tested on Android 16 and Android 17.
- An arm64 device. The APK is universal across the included Android ABIs.
- Local network access to the console.
- Installation from unknown sources enabled for sideloading.

The Android release APK is signed with a self-signed release key, not distributed through
Google Play. Android 17 local-network access uses the legacy target-SDK behavior because
the app targets SDK 36.

## Installation

Download the appropriate artifact from the project's Releases page.

| Platform | Artifact |
|---|---|
| macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) | `Y2JB.Installer_<version>_macos-universal.dmg` |
| Windows x64 | `y2jb-installer_<version>_windows-x64.zip` |
| Linux amd64 | `Y2JB.Installer_<version>_linux-amd64.AppImage` |
| Linux arm64 | `Y2JB.Installer_<version>_linux-aarch64.AppImage` |
| Android | `y2jb-installer_<version>_android-universal.apk` |

### macOS

Open the DMG and drag the application to **Applications**. The build is ad-hoc signed but not notarized. On first launch, right-click the application and choose **Open**, or allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.

### Windows

Extract the ZIP and run `y2jb-installer.exe`. No installer or administrator rights are required. If SmartScreen appears, choose **More info → Run anyway**.

### Linux

Make the AppImage executable and run it. The AppImage requires FUSE; use `--appimage-extract-and-run` if FUSE is unavailable. The AppImage includes GitHub Releases update information and can be updated with AppImageUpdate; the matching `.zsync` file is published next to it.

### Android

Download the APK and open it on the device, allowing installation from unknown sources when prompted. The APK is self-signed and intended for sideloading. The payload API is plain HTTP on the local network, so use the app only on a trusted LAN. See [Android](docs/ANDROID.md) for build and signing details.

## Usage

1. Start the exploit and the ELF loader on the console.
2. Open the application, scan the LAN, and select the console. If only the loader answers, click **Send payload** to start the embedded payload.
3. **Accounts** — activate a local user, then run the fake sign-in; the application uploads `np-fake-signin-ps5.elf`, sends it to the loader, and removes the console-side copy.
4. **YouTube** — select the region. The application detects the firmware, selects the matching build, fetches and verifies both PKGs, joins them, uploads the result, and starts the installation. The merged PKG is deleted when the job finishes.
5. **Y2JB** — select a `download0.dat` release, fetch it, and upload it. The panel reports the release installed on the console, the release cached locally, and whether an update is available.
6. **Block updates** — confirm the dialog. The payload edits `/system_data/priv/mms/appinfo.db` in place, keeps a timestamped backup, and reboots the console. This is the final setup action; the same reboot also applies account activation and fake sign-in.
7. Disconnect the console from the internet, then launch YouTube to trigger Y2JB. Opening YouTube online can show the sign-in screen and overwrite `download0.dat`.

The payload does not survive a reboot. To perform another action after restarting, start the exploit and the ELF loader again and resend the payload from the application.

## Data and Persistence

### Application

Downloaded files and application settings are stored per user:

| Platform | Cache and downloads | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/dev.y2jb.installer` | `~/Library/Application Support/dev.y2jb.installer` |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\dev.y2jb.installer` | `%APPDATA%\dev.y2jb.installer` |
| Linux | `~/.local/share/dev.y2jb.installer` | `~/.config/dev.y2jb.installer` |
| Android | App-private storage | App-private storage |

The cache can be cleared from the application. Removing the application does not remove these directories.

### Console

- The placed file at `/user/download/PPSA01650/download0.dat` is the intended Y2JB artifact.
- Timestamped `appinfo.db` backups are kept under `/data/y2jb-installer/store`.
- Temporary uploads live under `/data/y2jb-installer/tmp` and are removed after use or by the startup cleanup.
- No installer settings, credentials, or resume state are stored on the console.

## Security Model

- The payload API listens on all interfaces on port **47291** and has **no authentication**. Use it only on a trusted local network and never expose the port to the internet.
- Every download is verified: Sony PKGs against pinned SHA-256 hashes, GitHub assets against their published digests. TLS verification is relaxed only for the pinned Sony host that requires it; the SHA-256 check remains the trust anchor.
- Uploads use fixed slots. The client cannot choose a destination path, and every upload is length- and hash-verified before it is moved into place.
- The payload performs a DNS lookup and TCP reachability probe solely to detect whether the console has effective internet access; it has no general internet client.
- YouTube updates are blocked by editing the original database in place, preserving its ownership, permissions, and inode. Backups are deliberately retained; there is no restore operation.
- The application stores no PSN credentials and sends no telemetry.

## Building from Source

### Prerequisites

- [PS5 payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) with clang/lld 18.
- Node.js 24.
- Rust stable.
- GNU Make, a POSIX shell, and the platform's [Tauri prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/).

### Build

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
make test                 # host tests; no PS5 SDK required
scripts/build_deps.sh     # libmicrohttpd and SQLite for the payload
make payload              # build/y2jb-installer.elf
make app                  # UI, payload, and desktop application
```

The payload ELF is embedded in the desktop binary, so the deployed payload always matches the application that sent it.

CI resolves the latest PS5 payload SDK release at build time and verifies the ZIP against GitHub's published SHA-256 digest. Set `SDK_TAG` to pin a release when debugging.

Platform prerequisites and release builds are in [Building](docs/BUILDING.md).

## Testing

```sh
make test
npm --prefix ui run check
npm --prefix ui run build
cargo test --manifest-path app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
```

The host and unit tests run without a console. Network-dependent tests are described in [Testing](docs/TESTING.md).

Y2JB Installer for Windows
==========================

This ZIP contains one executable. There is nothing to install; double-click
y2jb-installer.exe.

Requirements
------------
- Windows 10 (1803 or later) or Windows 11.
- Microsoft Edge WebView2. It is built into Windows 11 and installed with
  Edge on Windows 10. If it is missing, install the Evergreen WebView2
  Runtime from Microsoft.
- The PS5 must be on firmware 4.03-13.60, with kernel read/write access and
  an ELF loader listening on port 9021. Firmware 11.40 is not supported by
  the Y2JB autoloader.

No administrator rights, WSL, MSYS2, Python or .NET are needed. The
executable carries its own runtime except for WebView2, which is part of
Windows.

First launch
------------
Windows SmartScreen will warn that the app is unsigned. Choose "More info",
then "Run anyway". The build is not code-signed.

Where data is kept
------------------
Downloads and settings live in:

    %APPDATA%\dev.y2jb.installer

Delete that folder to reclaim the space or start fresh. Remove the app by
deleting the executable.

Before launching YouTube
------------------------
Disconnect the console from the internet first. Opening YouTube online can
show the sign-in screen and overwrite download0.dat, which breaks the Y2JB
setup and requires reinstalling it.

Safety
------
The app talks to Sony's package servers and GitHub from this PC, and to the
console on your local network. It does not contain an exploit. The payload it
sends runs only on a console that already has kernel read/write access.

Automatically loads the kernel exploit and your elf payloads.
Supports PS5 firmwares 4.03-13.60

Other Autoloaders:
WebKit | BD-JB | Lua

## How to Use There are two ways to use the autoloader: ### 🟢 Option 1: Payload Manager If no `autoload.txt` config is found, the autoloader will automatically launch **[Payload Manager](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager)** — a fully-featured PS5 payload manager with a web UI. This lets you configure and send payloads directly from your browser, without needing to manually set up config files or transfer ELF files ahead of time. Just run the autoloader — if there's nothing configured, Payload Manager starts automatically. > **Note:** Payload Manager also has its own built-in autoload feature, which lets you configure payloads to load automatically on startup — all managed through its web UI. This is separate from the `autoload.txt` mechanism described below. --- ### ⚙️ Option 2: Manual Config (`autoload.txt`) For a fixed, automated payload chain, you can configure payloads manually: - Create a directory named `ps5_autoloader`. - Inside this directory, place your `.elf` / `.bin` files, and an `autoload.txt` file. - In `autoload.txt`, list the files you want to load, one filename per line. - Filenames are case-sensitive — ensure each name exactly matches the file. - You can add lines like `!1000` to make the loader wait 1000 ms before sending the next payload. - Put the `ps5_autoloader` directory in one of these locations (priority order - highest first): - Root of a USB drive - Internal drive: `/data/ps5_autoloader` > **Note:** When an `autoload.txt` config is found, Payload Manager is **not** launched automatically. If you also want Payload Manager available, place `pldmgr.elf` in your `ps5_autoloader` directory and add it to `autoload.txt`. ## How to Update You can update the autoloader by simply placing **`y2jb_update.zip`** (from the [Releases page](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5_y2jb_autoloader/releases)) on the **root** of a USB drive, and starting the app. ## Setup Instructions Installation is the same as the original [Y2JB](https://github.com/Gezine/Y2JB/blob/main/README.md) (remote loader). ### Jailbroken PS5 (Webkit, Lua, BD-JB) Install YouTube (`PPSA01650` / `PPSA01651` / `PPSA01652`): | Firmware | YouTube Version | | :--- | :--- | | **4.03 – 12.40** | `v01.000.003` | | **12.60 – 13.20** | `v01.000.030` | | **13.40 – 13.60** | `v01.009.253` | Then FTP `download0.dat` from Releases to `/user/download/PPSA0165*/`. ### Non-Jailbroken PS5 You might find a system backup with pre-configured Autoloader (I don't distribute such backups). You can also restore [Y2JB](https://github.com/Gezine/Y2JB) (remote loader) system backup, and then: - use FTP to place `download0.dat` from releases page in `/user/download/PPSA01650` - or install separate YT app from different region, and use FTP to place `download0.dat` from releases page in `/user/download/PPSA0165*/` > [!NOTE] > Relapse requires an active network interface (Wi-Fi or Ethernet connected to a local network; Internet access is not required). On FW 7.00–10.01, it is used when a network interface is detected (falling back to Lapse otherwise). On FW 10.20–13.60, an active network interface is required. ## Additional Info
How to have different autoload configs for multiple YT apps? If you want to use multiple YT apps from different regions, name your directory ps5_autoloader_[TITLE_ID], e.g. ps5_autoloader_PPSA01650 this will allow you to have different autoload.txt files for each app (these directories always take precedence over the generic ps5_autoloader directory)
How to use custom ELF Loader version? By default, the autoloader uses a custom version of **elfldr** that only accepts connections from the PS5 itself (localhost). This improves security by preventing other devices on your network from sending payloads to your console. If you want to use a "normal" ELF Loader that allows sending payloads from any device: 1. Place your custom ELF Loader (e.g. `elfldr.elf`) in the `ps5_autoloader` directory. 2. Add `elfldr.elf` to your `autoload.txt`. 3. **Note**: If you are loading other payloads right after `elfldr.elf` in your `autoload.txt`, add a sleep command immediately after it (like `!4000` to sleep for 4 seconds) to give the new ELF Loader time to start up and listen before subsequent payloads are sent. Example `autoload.txt`: ```text # Load custom ELF Loader elfldr.elf # Give it 4 seconds to start up (only needed if sending more payloads) !4000 # Send other payloads etaHEN.elf ```

documentation.text:
# Bundled menu library

128 packs, 162 compiled scripts, all in PS4 (little-endian) GSC format.

Layout: `library/<mode>/<Pack name>/<script slot>` where mode is `mp` (Multiplayer), `zm` (Zombies) or `gm` (Game Modes, injected into the Multiplayer process). The path under the pack folder is the exact game script that gets replaced, for example `maps/mp/gametypes/_clientids.gsc`. A pack with several scripts is injected as a unit; if one script fails the others are rolled back.

Each pack has a `NOTES.txt`: where the file came from, which platform it was compiled for, and every repair the converter applied. Read it before injecting a pack for the first time.

Sources: community BO2 GSC releases collected in the Fortis BO2 GSC Studio library. They were converted from their PS3 / Xbox 360 (and two PC, two source) originals to PS4 bytecode with that tool's converter, then checked with SPOMEN's parser. `JR JS V8` (Multiplayer) is not included: its `createmenu()` jump exceeds the PS4 bytecode range and cannot be converted.

Six Game Modes files had custom file names with no matching game script; they are installed as `maps/mp/_development_dvars.gsc` and marked in their notes.

# DayBreak V1.1.2 – BO3 Zombies SPRX (PS4 / PS5)

**Game:** Black Ops III – CUSA02624 (V1.33)
**Needs:** GoldHEN (PS4) or NexHEN (PS5)

Lan Spoof Works on MP/ZM/CP

link to keep checking if it gets updated download new file
https://github.com/xexpoiiison/DayBreak-SPRX-Release

## Fixed in V1.1.2
- **Set Round now sticks.** Picking a round jumped to current+1 instead (round 2 → 3). It now sets BO3's real round counter, so it lands on the round you pick.
- **Pack-a-Punch Current Weapon** now works on guns the map's upgrade table misses, like the **Razorback**.

## Fixed in V1.1.1
- **PS5 / NexHEN autoload:** DayBreak didn't show up when set to `?autoload=true` in NexHEN (no load box, no menu), but worked when loaded from the Plugin Loader at the main menu. NexHEN autoload injects the moment the game starts, before BO3 is ready, and DayBreak gave up. It now waits for the main menu and hooks in then, the same as the Plugin Loader. It also keeps retrying its startup and controller hook instead of giving up, and shows the load box within 20 seconds on the main menu even if the X on "Press X to start" was missed.
- **Clearer messages:** if another plugin already hooked BO3 or took over the controller, DayBreak now says so instead of "game version doesn't match".
- PS4 with GoldHEN loads the same as before.

## Install (PS4 – GoldHEN)
1. Download `DayBreak.sprx`
2. With FTP, copy it to:
   `/data/GoldHEN/plugins/DayBreak.sprx`
3. Open `/data/GoldHEN/plugins.ini` (create it if it isn't there) and add:
   ```ini
   [CUSA02290]
   /data/GoldHEN/plugins/DayBreak.sprx
   ```
4. Restart BO3.

## Install (PS5 – NexHEN)
1. Download `DayBreak.sprx`
2. With FTP, copy it to:
   `/data/nexHEN/plugins/DayBreak.sprx`
3. In NexHEN's `plugins.ini`, add:
   ```ini
   [CUSA02290]
   /data/nexHEN/plugins/DayBreak.sprx?autoload=true
   ```
   Or leave off `?autoload=true` and enable it through NexHEN's Plugin Loader.
4. Start BO3.

## Use
- After "Press X to start" it asks **"Would you like to load DayBreak ZM SPRX?"** Pick **Yes**.
- **L1 + R1** opens the menu (Pre Game Menu on the main menu, Full Menu in a match).
- **D-pad** moves, **X** selects, **O** goes back, **Left / Right** changes values.
- **Verified players:** hold **L1** and tap **R1** (or **L1 + Triangle**) to open their menu.

## Coming in V1.2
- **Stats for all modes** (Multiplayer, Campaign and Zombies), done right in the SPRX, no GSC injection: level, prestige, unlocks, liquid divinium, clan tag and more.

## Problems
- Nothing shows up: check the path and `plugins.ini`, and make sure your game is CUSA02290 on the latest patch.
- Running other BO3 plugins? Try DayBreak by itself first, and only list it once in `plugins.ini`.
- Questions: Discord / X **@xexpoiiison**

Created By: XeX Poiiison

documentation.text:
CD Player - PPSA98427
====================

A native PS5 audio CD player with a minimal digital interface.
CD Player appears in the Media section of the PS5 home screen.
Its title ID is independent of other homebrew applications.

INSTALLATION
Import PPSA98427.zip using your usual homebrew installation method.
The ZIP contains one PPSA98427 folder. Copy it into /data/homebrew so that
eboot.bin is at /data/homebrew/PPSA98427/eboot.bin, without another nested folder.
Update the application only while CD Player is closed.
Version 1.1.2 fixes an oversized storage reservation. If an older installation
still occupies about 18 GB, remove CD Player through the PS5 storage settings
and install the new release again. Replacing files alone does not shrink the
existing allocation. Reinstallation may reset settings and cached artwork.
The package preserves the open permissions required by the homebrew loader.

USB CD DRIVES AND APPLE SUPERDRIVE
CD Player reads audio CDs from USB optical drives through FreeBSD CAM.
Apple SuperDrive initialization and software disc ejection are included.
The Eject button is provided especially for Apple USB SuperDrive, which has
no physical eject button. Press Triangle or select the Eject icon to remove
the disc. The same command remains available for other compatible USB drives.
No Apple Boot Camp driver binaries are included.

Start the console with the USB drive empty, then insert an audio CD.
PSSwanStation documents drive lockups during console boot with a disc inserted.
An active compatible PS5 homebrew environment is required. The included
one-shot access helper is restricted to PPSA98427. A local ELF loader on
port 9021 may be needed by the helper. Firmware compatibility is separate
from successful compilation.

CONTROLS
D-pad: navigate. Cross: select. Square: play/pause. Triangle: eject.
L1/R1: previous/next track. L2/R2: seek backward/forward by 10 seconds.
Touchpad: fullscreen visualizer. Options: settings. Circle: back.
L3 on the album page: turn the case over; press again to return to its front.
Right stick up/down: adjust the master volume from any screen.
Hold Options + Circle to close the application.
A Play icon in the accent color replaces the number of the track currently playing.
The six icon buttons offer previous track, play/pause, next track,
visualizer, settings and eject. The Show Eject button toggle hides the Eject
icon and lets the other five buttons fill the same total width without
resizing their icons. The Triangle eject shortcut remains available.

Select the album cover to open album notes when a description is available.
Up/down scroll the cover, headings and description together with smooth motion.
Back stays fixed in the footer. Reduce motion disables
the scrolling animation as well as other optional interface motion.

VISUALIZERS
The catalog contains 152 original iwrzwr drawing studies and nine individual
studies derived from its compositions. One visualizer appears at a time.
Left/right changes the effect in fullscreen; settings also offer a selector.
Shuffle visualizers chooses another effect when the audible track changes,
without repeating the current effect. The choice and toggle are saved.
The effect name and controller hints fade together after two seconds idle.
Original drawing programs run locally in QuickJS and are rendered through
Prospero Homebrew UI/OpenGL. No browser is required.

AUDIO AND SETTINGS
Audio CDs provide stereo PCM at 44.1 kHz, resampled to 48 kHz for AudioOut.
The ten-band equalizer, volume, gapless playback and optional 7.1 upmix can
be adjusted during playback. Upmix derives surround sound from stereo; it
does not turn the CD into an original multichannel recording. The upmix
control is unavailable when AudioOut only accepts stereo output.

Speaker setup opens within the settings drawer and controls all eight speakers
independently: front left/right, center, surround left/right, side left/right,
and subwoofer (LFE). Each ranges from mute to +24 dB. 0 dB keeps its original
level; fronts stay unchanged unless their own controls are adjusted.
Previous upmix gains carry over to the individual speakers, including mute.
Front controls also work in stereo; additional speakers require 7.1 upmix.
Gain changes are smoothed, with peak protection on generated or boosted channels.

LYRICS
Press R3 in the fullscreen visualizer to switch to lyrics, or back again.
Timed lyrics highlight the current phrase and scroll it smoothly to the
center, following playback, pause and seeking. When only untimed lyrics are
available, use the D-pad to scroll. Availability depends on the track.
Lyrics are provided by LRCLIB and cached after the first online lookup.
Temporary server errors trigger automatic retries while the loading message
stays visible. Leaving lyrics or changing tracks cancels further retries.
No song lyrics or recordings are bundled with the app.
Returning to the current track's loaded lyrics opens them without a loading flash.
Circle returns directly to the album page from either fullscreen mode.
Reopening fullscreen restores the last lyrics or visualizer choice.

Autoplay disc starts the first audio track after a disc is detected. It is off
by default and can be enabled in settings. Changing the toggle does not start
a disc that is already present.

Equalizer bands and enable state, upmix and its channel gains, gapless playback, autoplay, volume, reduce
motion, selected visualizer, shuffle, Eject button visibility and accent color are saved
automatically.
Changes are checked for saving once per second and restored at the next launch.
Application updates preserve these settings outside the installation folder.
Accent color offers 40 named colors with a swatch. Changes apply immediately.
Visualizer colors follow the same accent. Right-stick volume changes leave
open settings and album panels in place.

ALBUM METADATA
Internet access is needed for online album information and covers.
MusicBrainz identifies the disc and its editions; Cover Art Archive supplies
artwork. CD-Text offers local titles when present. Album notes use MusicBrainz
annotations or the English Wikipedia page linked through MusicBrainz/Wikidata.
The cover is selectable only when a real description is available.
Online responses and artwork are cached. Source attribution is retained in
the cache metadata and project documentation.
No recordings or cover-art files from the test CDs are bundled in the app.
Printed disc labels, back covers and spines are downloaded for the selected
edition when available. Each image fades in independently. Missing images
leave that surface blank. A combined back/spine scan is split into its
central inlay and a narrow folded edge for the three-dimensional case.

VIDEO AND LOGS
The tested Media configuration runs at approximately 60 Hz on the console.
The renderer requests a higher rate, but a 120 Hz request is not a guarantee
of 120 fps. The session log records the accepted mode and measured frame rate.
Settings, caches and session.log are kept at /data/cdplayer-PPSA98427.
Without access to /data, the fallback is /download0/cdplayer in the app sandbox.
The startup log is at:
/mnt/sandbox/PPSA98427_000/download0/hui/dev/app.log

VALIDATION
Apple SuperDrive playback, online artwork and album descriptions have been
confirmed on the owner's PS5 running firmware 13.60. This is not a claim of
compatibility with every firmware, USB drive or surround audio setup.
Host checks cover CD commands and parsing, metadata, DSP, resampling,
gapless playback, ejection, animation and saved-preference restoration.
SHA256SUMS.txt lists the files in this package.

CREDITS
Based on PSSwanStation by Press5elect.
Prospero Homebrew UI and PS5 Native App Boilerplate: BlackBearReloaded.
Graphics: ps5-opengl, Mesa and OpenGNM PSBC.
Visualizers: iwrzwr Visual Archive by Kagan Yaldizkaya.
Doto: Oliver Lalan. Inter fallback font: Rasmus Andersson.
SuperDrive initialization protocol: Alfredo Sandoval.
Metadata: MusicBrainz, Cover Art Archive, Wikidata and Wikipedia contributors.
See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and licenses/ for all component licenses.

VERSION 1.1.0
The track list follows the audible track only when it changes; manual browsing
remains free. The Eject hint follows the Show Eject button setting.
OLED mode hides fullscreen text after two seconds and slowly shifts effects.
After one idle minute with playback stopped it shows a black screen; any input
restores the picture. OLED mode is remembered between launches.
Visualizer timing follows the display, with a compiled frame function and
reusable buffers. Terminal effects include monospaced box-drawing characters.

VERSION 1.1.2
Music keeps playing when the controller turns off or disconnects, including
when the system temporarily takes controller input. Play/Pause remains manual.
Speaker setup provides saved, independent gain controls for all eight outputs.
R3 switches between the fullscreen visualizer and lyrics. Timed phrases scroll
with playback when available; untimed lyrics can be scrolled manually.

Enable the background, select LushModz.bg157, and Save Background Settings.

Refresh Images reloads the selected image and rescans up to 32 prepared files.

This renderer uses a coarse, bounded approximation of your image made from

On Windows the converter uses System.Drawing if Pillow is unavailable.
On other platforms install Pillow first. Copy the resulting .bg157 file into
this folder, then use Refresh Images and select it in the menu.
Use simple logos or bold shapes for the clearest result at this drawing budget.

/data/Expulsion/LUA-Scripts/MountMod.lua

In Expulsion:
Misc Options > LUA Scripts > Refresh / Search for .lua Scripts
Select MountMod.lua > Enable Script, then close Expulsion.

MountMod controls:
R1 + D-pad Down: show/hide MountMod menu.
D-pad Up/Down: select Cow, Deer or Mountain Lion.
X: activate selected option (spawns animal and mounts it).
Circle: hide MountMod menu.
While riding: left stick moves, hold X runs, Triangle dismounts/removes animal.
Stop the script from Expulsion to remove its animal and detach the rider.

The port rides animals spawned by this script; it does not mount nearby players.
The original keyboard GUI and indefinite wait loops are replaced by the PS4 API
and Expulsion's asynchronous animal-riding backend. MountMod by Ideo; PS4 port
for Expulsion. Original files retained under research/mountmod/original.

Browser:
Refresh rescans the folder. Running Scripts lists enabled scripts with Stop.
Each script has Enable, Reload and Stop. Maximum four active scripts.
Only .lua text files directly inside this folder are scanned; subfolders skipped.
File limit 64 KiB, 128 listed files, 2 MiB Lua memory per script.
Scripts start only when you enable them; no automatic startup.
Errors and instruction/memory budget failures stop the script and clean up its
owned animal. Existing native animal rides are not owned by the Lua script.

Compatibility:
This is embedded Lua 5.4.8 with Expulsion Lua API v1, not the old PC Lua plugin.
Other PC scripts must be ported; GAMEPLAY/AI/UI/Libs/Keys/wait are not provided.
A script returns a table with optional init(), tick(), stop() functions.
See API.md for the supported functions. Arbitrary native pointers are not exposed.

Local runtime, browser, controller and cleanup tests passed. Real PS4 behavior
has not been verified. Keep LUA-LICENSE.txt with redistributed builds.

LUSH MODZ FUN V1 MENU
Copy LushModzFunV1Menu.lua into the same LUA-Scripts folder. Requires the
updated PRX bundled with this release (rect/icon/fun Lua API extensions).
Enable it from Misc Options > LUA Scripts and close the main Expulsion menu.
L1 + D-pad Down: show/hide. Up/Down: select. X: activate. Circle: back/hide.
Left/Right: adjust. Square: cycle six palettes. Triangle: cycle three designs.
Includes Self Playground, Vehicle Arcade, World Mood, Animal Rides and
Design Studio. Appearance settings last until the script is reloaded.
Vehicle actions require the driver seat and network control. Launch/boost
power is adjustable. Weather/time are local requests; session scripts may
restore them. Hiding the menu does not stop a ride; Triangle dismounts.
Stopping/reloading the script removes only the animal ride it owns.
One-shot changes such as paint, clothing, time and weather remain applied.
Avoid operating multiple Lua menus at once because controller inputs are shared.
Expulsion saves Expulsion_Map.txt here. Keep existing maps when updating.

Expulsion Indoor Skatepark
Copy indoor-skatepark.map157 into /data/Expulsion/Maps/ on PS4.
Use Map Mods > Modded Maps from PC > Indoor Skatepark.
Mansion, Military Sea Base and SidehouseX have been removed. Their old files on PS4 are no longer used.
Rebuild the retained file: python tools/convert_pc_maps157.py
Generated stunt maps remain built in.

EXPULSION V7.0 - By Lush Modz
GTA V PS4 update 1.57 - All-in-one USA / EUR PRX

PS4 INSTALL
1. Fully close GTA V. Enable GoldHEN FTP and game plugins on the PS4.
2. Extract the ZIP and open Expulsion V7.0/PS4/.
   Merge PS4/data/ into console /data/ and PS4/user/ into console /user/.
   Preserve existing settings, outfits and custom files; skip conflicting samples.
3. Install the single shared menu file at:
   /data/GoldHEN/plugins/LushModz-Expulsion-1.57.prx
   This same PRX is used for both USA and EUR. No region-specific copy is needed.
4. Edit /data/GoldHEN/plugins.ini (the filename is plugins.ini).
   Add the entry matching your installed game's title ID:

   USA - CUSA00419:
   [CUSA00419]
   /data/GoldHEN/plugins/LushModz-Expulsion-1.57.prx

   EUR - CUSA00411:
   [CUSA00411]
   /data/GoldHEN/plugins/LushModz-Expulsion-1.57.prx

   You can keep only your game's entry, or keep both entries above.
   At least the MATCHING title section and PRX path must be present.
   A USA-only entry will not load the EUR game, or vice versa.
   Use the game's title ID, not your PSN account region.
   Both sections point to the same file; you only update that one PRX.

   If your title section already exists, update its Expulsion entry instead
   of duplicating the section. Replace any old region-folder or alias path.
   Enable only one Expulsion entry per title. Preserve unrelated settings.
   plugins.ini.example is a reference, not a replacement configuration.
   If using the supported Velora build, keep Velora before Expulsion.
5. Launch GTA V again. Default menu combo: Square + D-pad Right.
   D-pad navigates, X selects, Circle returns. Saved custom binds take precedence.

INDOOR SKATEPARK
Keep /data/Expulsion/Maps/indoor-skatepark.map157 installed from this package.

IF THE MENU DOES NOT LOAD
Check update 1.57, the matching CUSA section, the exact PRX path and GoldHEN
plugin enablement. Remove duplicate Expulsion entries for the same title.
A hook/signature rejection means the executable failed compatibility checks;
do not disable those checks. EUR console testing remains required.

  PC Lua scripts need adaptation to Expulsion Lua API v1.

  Legacy assets; custom popup icons are disabled.

No files were uploaded to your console while creating this package.
